nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditIPsecQuickMode
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by Internet Key Exchange protocol (IKE) and Authenticated Internet Protocol (AuthIP) during Quick Mode negotiations.

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditLogoff
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by the closing of a logon session. These events occur on the computer that was accessed.

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditLogon
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by user account logon attempts on the computer.

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditNetworkPolicyServer
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by RADIUS (IAS) and Network Access Protection (NAP) user access requests.

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditOtherLogonLogoffEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit other logon/logoff-related events that aren't covered in the "Logon/Logoff" policy setting such as the following: Terminal Services session disconnections.

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditSpecialLogon
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by special logons such as the following: The use of a special logon, which is a logon that has administrator-equivalent privileges and can be…

nodes.name: AccountLogonLogoff_AuditUserDeviceClaims
nodes.description: This policy allows you to audit user and device claims information in the user's logon token. Events in this subcategory are generated on the computer on which a logon session is created.

nodes.name: AccountLogon_AuditCredentialValidation
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by validation tests on user account logon credentials.

nodes.name: AccountLogon_AuditKerberosAuthenticationService
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by Kerberos authentication ticket-granting ticket (TGT) requests.

nodes.name: AccountLogon_AuditKerberosServiceTicketOperations
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by Kerberos authentication ticket-granting ticket (TGT) requests submitted for user accounts.

nodes.name: AccountLogon_AuditOtherAccountLogonEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by responses to credential requests submitted for a user account logon that aren't credential validation or Kerberos tickets.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditApplicationGroupManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to application groups such as the following: Application group is created, changed, or deleted.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditComputerAccountManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to computer accounts such as when a computer account is created, changed, or deleted.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditDistributionGroupManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to distribution groups such as the following: Distribution group is created, changed, or deleted.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditOtherAccountManagementEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by other user account changes that aren't covered in this category, such as the following: The password hash of a user account was accessed.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditSecurityGroupManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to security groups such as the following: Security group is created, changed, or deleted.

nodes.name: AccountManagement_AuditUserAccountManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit changes to user accounts. Events include the following: A user account is created, changed, deleted; renamed, disabled, enabled, locked out, or unlocked.

nodes.name: DSAccess_AuditDetailedDirectoryServiceReplication
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by detailed Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) replication between domain controllers. Volume: High.

nodes.name: DSAccess_AuditDirectoryServiceAccess
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) object is accessed.

nodes.name: DSAccess_AuditDirectoryServiceChanges
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to objects in Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS).

nodes.name: DSAccess_AuditDirectoryServiceReplication
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit replication between two Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain controllers.

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditDPAPIActivity
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when encryption or decryption requests are made to the Data Protection application interface (DPAPI).

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditPNPActivity
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit when plug and play detects an external device.

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditProcessCreation
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when a process is created or starts. The name of the application or user that created the process is also audited.

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditProcessTermination
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when a process ends. If you configure this policy setting, an audit event is generated when a process ends.

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditRPCEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit inbound remote procedure call (RPC) connections. If you configure this policy setting, an audit event is generated when a remote RPC connection is attempted.

nodes.name: DetailedTracking_AuditTokenRightAdjusted
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by adjusting the privileges of a token. Volume: High.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditApplicationGenerated
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit applications that generate events using the Windows Auditing application programming interfaces (APIs).

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditCentralAccessPolicyStaging
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit access requests where the permission granted or denied by a proposed policy differs from the current central access policy on an object.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditCertificationServices
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) operations. AD CS operations include the following: AD CS startup/shutdown/backup/restore.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditDetailedFileShare
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit attempts to access files and folders on a shared folder.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditFileShare
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit attempts to access a shared folder. If you configure this policy setting, an audit event is generated when an attempt is made to access a shared folder.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditFileSystem
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit user attempts to access file system objects.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditFilteringPlatformConnection
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit connections that are allowed or blocked by the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP).

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditFilteringPlatformPacketDrop
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit packets that are dropped by Windows Filtering Platform (WFP). Volume: High.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditHandleManipulation
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when a handle to an object is opened or closed. Only objects with a matching system access control list (SACL) generate security audit events.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditKernelObject
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit attempts to access the kernel, which include mutexes and semaphores.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditOtherObjectAccessEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by the management of task scheduler jobs or COM+ objects. For scheduler jobs, the following are audited: Job created. Job deleted. Job enabled.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditRegistry
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit attempts to access registry objects.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditRemovableStorage
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit user attempts to access file system objects on a removable storage device.

nodes.name: ObjectAccess_AuditSAM
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by attempts to access to Security Accounts Manager (SAM) objects. SAM objects include the following: SAM_ALIAS -- A local group.

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditAuthenticationPolicyChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to the authentication policy such as the following: Creation of forest and domain trusts. Modification of forest and domain trusts.

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditAuthorizationPolicyChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to the authorization policy such as the following: Assignment of user rights (privileges), such as SeCreateTokenPrivilege, that…

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditFilteringPlatformPolicyChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes to the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) such as the following: IPsec services status. Changes to IPsec policy settings.

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditMPSSVCRuleLevelPolicyChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes in policy rules used by the Microsoft Protection Service (MPSSVC). This service is used by Windows Firewall.

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditOtherPolicyChangeEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by other security policy changes that aren't audited in the policy change category, such as the following: Trusted Platform Module (TPM)…

nodes.name: PolicyChange_AuditPolicyChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit changes in the security audit policy settings such as the following: Settings permissions and audit settings on the Audit Policy object.

nodes.name: PrivilegeUse_AuditNonSensitivePrivilegeUse
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by the use of non-sensitive privileges (user rights).

nodes.name: PrivilegeUse_AuditOtherPrivilegeUseEvents
nodes.description: Not used.

nodes.name: PrivilegeUse_AuditSensitivePrivilegeUse
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated when sensitive privileges (user rights) are used such as the following: A privileged service is called.

nodes.name: System_AuditIPsecDriver
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by the IPsec filter driver such as the following: Startup and shutdown of the IPsec services.

nodes.name: System_AuditOtherSystemEvents
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit any of the following events: Startup and shutdown of the Windows Firewall service and driver. Security policy processing by the Windows Firewall Service.

nodes.name: System_AuditSecurityStateChange
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events generated by changes in the security state of the computer such as the following events: Startup and shutdown of the computer. Change of system time.

nodes.name: System_AuditSecuritySystemExtension
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events related to security system extensions or services such as the following: A security system extension, such as an authentication, notification, or…

nodes.name: System_AuditSystemIntegrity
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to audit events that violate the integrity of the security subsystem, such as the following: Events that couldn't be written to the event log because of a problem with…

nodes.name: AllowAadPasswordReset
nodes.description: Specifies whether password reset is enabled for Microsoft Entra accounts.

nodes.name: AllowEAPCertSSO
nodes.description: Allows an EAP cert-based authentication for a single sign-on (SSO) to access internal resources.

nodes.name: AllowFastReconnect
nodes.description: Allows EAP Fast Reconnect from being attempted for EAP Method TLS. Most restricted value is 0.

nodes.name: AllowSecondaryAuthenticationDevice
nodes.description: This policy allows users to use a companion device, such as a phone, fitness band, or IoT device, to sign-on to a desktop computer running Windows 10.

nodes.name: ConfigureWebSignInAllowedUrls
nodes.description: Specifies a list of URLs that are navigable in Web Sign-in based authentication scenarios. This policy specifies the list of domains that users can access in certain authentication scenarios.

nodes.name: ConfigureWebcamAccessDomainNames
nodes.description: Specifies a list of domains that are allowed to access the webcam in Web Sign-in based authentication scenarios. Note Web sign-in is only supported on Microsoft Entra joined PCs.

nodes.name: EnableFastFirstSignIn
nodes.description: Specifies whether new non-admin Microsoft Entra accounts should auto-connect to pre-created candidate local accounts.

allowedValues.description: The feature defaults to the existing SKU and device capabilities.
Enabled. Auto-connect new non-admin Microsoft Entra accounts to pre-configured candidate local accounts.
Disabled. Don't auto-connect new non-admin Microsoft Entra accounts to pre-configured local accounts.

nodes.name: EnablePasswordlessExperience
nodes.description: Specifies whether connected users on Microsoft Entra joined devices receive a Passwordless experience on Windows.

allowedValues.description: The feature defaults to the existing edition and device capabilities.
Enabled. The Passwordless experience will be enabled on Windows.
Disabled. The Passwordless experience won't be enabled on Windows.

nodes.name: EnableWebSignIn
nodes.description: Specifies whether web-based sign-in is allowed for signing in to Windows. Web sign-in is a credential provider that enables a web-based sign-in experience on Windows devices.

allowedValues.description: The feature defaults to the existing SKU and device capabilities.
Enabled. Web Sign-in will be enabled for signing in to Windows.
Disabled. Web Sign-in won't be enabled for signing in to Windows.

nodes.name: PreferredAadTenantDomainName
nodes.description: Specifies the preferred domain among available domains in the Microsoft Entra tenant.

nodes.name: DisallowAutoplayForNonVolumeDevices
nodes.description: This policy setting disallows AutoPlay for MTP devices like cameras or phones. If you enable this policy setting, AutoPlay isn't allowed for MTP devices like cameras or phones.

nodes.name: SetDefaultAutoRunBehavior
nodes.description: This policy setting sets the default behavior for Autorun commands. Autorun commands are generally stored in autorun.inf files. They often launch the installation program or other routines.

nodes.name: TurnOffAutoPlay
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to turn off the Autoplay feature. Autoplay begins reading from a drive as soon as you insert media in the drive.

nodes.name: BandwidthThrottlingEndTime
nodes.description: This policy setting limits the network bandwidth that Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) uses for background transfers. (This policy setting doesn't affect foreground transfers).

nodes.name: BandwidthThrottlingStartTime
nodes.description: This policy setting limits the network bandwidth that Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) uses for background transfers. (This policy setting doesn't affect foreground transfers).

nodes.name: BandwidthThrottlingTransferRate
nodes.description: This policy setting limits the network bandwidth that Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) uses for background transfers. (This policy setting doesn't affect foreground transfers).

nodes.name: CostedNetworkBehaviorBackgroundPriority
nodes.description: This policy setting defines the default behavior that the Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) uses for background transfers when the system is connected to a costed network (3G, etc.).

allowedValues.description: Transfer unless surcharge applies (when not roaming or over cap).
Transfer unless nearing limit (when not roaming or nearing cap).

nodes.name: CostedNetworkBehaviorForegroundPriority
nodes.description: This policy setting defines the default behavior that the Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) uses for background transfers when the system is connected to a costed network (3G, etc.).

allowedValues.description: Transfer unless surcharge applies (when not roaming or over cap).
Transfer unless nearing limit (when not roaming or nearing cap).

nodes.name: JobInactivityTimeout
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies the number of days a pending BITS job can remain inactive before the job is considered abandoned.

nodes.name: EncryptionMethod
nodes.description: This policy specifies the BitLocker Drive Encryption method and cipher strength.

nodes.name: AllowAdvertising
nodes.description: Specifies whether the device can send out Bluetooth advertisements. If this isn't set or it's deleted, the default value of 1 (Allow) is used. Most restricted value is 0.

allowedValues.description: Not allowed. When set to 0, the device won't send out advertisements. To verify, use any Bluetooth LE app and enable it to do advertising. Then, verify that the advertisement isn't received by the peripheral.

Allowed. When set to 1, the device will send out advertisements. To verify, use any Bluetooth LE app and enable it to do advertising. Then, verify that the advertisement is received by the peripheral.

nodes.name: AllowDiscoverableMode
nodes.description: Specifies whether other Bluetooth-enabled devices can discover the device. If this isn't set or it's deleted, the default value of 1 (Allow) is used. Most restricted value is 0.

allowedValues.description: Not allowed. When set to 0, other devices won't be able to detect the device. To verify, open the Bluetooth control panel on the device. Then, go to another Bluetooth-enabled device, open the Bluetooth control panel, and verify that you can't see the name of the device.

Allowed. When set to 1, other devices will be able to detect the device. To verify, open the Bluetooth control panel on the device. Then, go to another Bluetooth-enabled device, open the Bluetooth control panel and verify that you can discover it.

nodes.name: AllowPrepairing
nodes.description: Specifies whether to allow specific bundled Bluetooth peripherals to automatically pair with the host device.

nodes.name: AllowPromptedProximalConnections
nodes.description: This policy allows the IT admin to block users on these managed devices from using Swift Pair and other proximity based scenarios.

allowedValues.description: Disallow. Block users on these managed devices from using Swift Pair and other proximity based scenarios.
Allow. Allow users on these managed devices to use Swift Pair and other proximity based scenarios.

nodes.name: LocalDeviceName
nodes.description: Sets the local Bluetooth device name. If this is set, the value that it's set to will be used as the Bluetooth device name. To verify the policy is set, open the Bluetooth control panel on the device.

nodes.name: ServicesAllowedList
nodes.description: Set a list of allowable services and profiles. String hex formatted array of Bluetooth service UUIDs in canonical format, delimited by semicolons.

nodes.name: SetMinimumEncryptionKeySize
nodes.description: There are multiple levels of encryption strength when pairing Bluetooth devices. This policy helps prevent weaker devices cryptographically being used in high security environments.

nodes.name: AllowAddressBarDropdown
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether the Address bar drop-down functionality is available in Microsoft Edge.

allowedValues.description: Prevented/not allowed. Hide the Address bar drop-down functionality and disable the Show search and site suggestions as I type toggle in Settings.
Allowed. Show the Address bar drop-down list and make it available.

nodes.name: AllowAutofill
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can use Autofill to automatically fill in form fields while using Microsoft Edge. By default, employees can choose whether to use Autofill.

nodes.name: AllowBrowser
nodes.description: This policy is deprecated.

nodes.name: AllowConfigurationUpdateForBooksLibrary
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether Microsoft Edge can automatically update the configuration data for the Books Library.

allowedValues.description: Allowed. Microsoft Edge updates the configuration data for the Books Library automatically.

nodes.name: AllowCookies
nodes.description: This setting lets you configure how to work with cookies. If you enable this setting, you must also decide whether to: Allow all cookies (default): Allows all cookies from all websites.

allowedValues.description: Block all cookies from all sites.
Block only cookies from third party websites.
Allow all cookies from all sites.

nodes.name: AllowDeveloperTools
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether F12 Developer Tools are available on Microsoft Edge. If you enable or don't configure this setting, the F12 Developer Tools are available in Microsoft Edge.

nodes.name: AllowDoNotTrack
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can send Do Not Track requests to websites that ask for tracking info.

nodes.name: AllowExtensions
nodes.description: This setting lets you decide whether employees can load extensions in Microsoft Edge. If you enable or don't configure this setting, employees can use Microsoft Edge Extensions.

nodes.name: AllowFlash
nodes.description: This setting lets you decide whether employees can run Adobe Flash in Microsoft Edge. If you enable or don't configure this setting, employees can use Adobe Flash.

nodes.name: AllowFlashClickToRun
nodes.description: If you enable or don't configure the Adobe Flash Click-to-Run setting, Microsoft Edge will require a user to click the Click-to-Run button, to click the content, or for the site to appear on the…

allowedValues.description: Load and run Adobe Flash content automatically.
Does not load or run Adobe Flash content automatically. Requires action from the user.

nodes.name: AllowFullScreenMode
nodes.description: With this policy, you can specify whether to allow full-screen mode, which shows only the web content and hides the Microsoft Edge UI. If enabled or not configured, full-screen mode is available for…

nodes.name: AllowInPrivate
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can browse using InPrivate website browsing. If you enable or don't configure this setting, employees can use InPrivate website browsing.

nodes.name: AllowMicrosoftCompatibilityList
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether to use the Microsoft Compatibility List (a Microsoft-provided list that helps sites with known compatibility issues to display properly) in Microsoft Edge.

nodes.name: AllowPasswordManager
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can save their passwords locally, using Password Manager. By default, Password Manager is turned on.

nodes.name: AllowPopups
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether to turn on Pop-up Blocker. By default, Pop-up Blocker is turned on.

allowedValues.description: Turn off Pop-up Blocker letting pop-up windows open.
Turn on Pop-up Blocker stopping pop-up windows from opening.

nodes.name: AllowPrelaunch
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether Microsoft Edge can pre-launch during Windows sign in, when the system is idle, and each time Microsoft Edge is closed.

nodes.name: AllowPrinting
nodes.description: With this policy, you can restrict whether printing web content in Microsoft Edge is allowed. If enabled, printing is allowed. If disabled, printing isn't allowed.

nodes.name: AllowSavingHistory
nodes.description: Microsoft Edge saves your user's browsing history, which is made up of info about the websites they visit, on their devices.

nodes.name: AllowSearchEngineCustomization
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether users can change their search engine. If you disable this setting, users can't add new search engines or change the default used in the address bar.

nodes.name: AllowSearchSuggestionsinAddressBar
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether search suggestions appear in the Address bar of Microsoft Edge.

allowedValues.description: Prevented/Not allowed. Hide the search suggestions.

nodes.name: AllowSideloadingOfExtensions
nodes.description: Sideloading installs and runs unverified extensions in Microsoft Edge. With this policy, you can specify whether unverified extensions can be sideloaded in Microsoft Edge.

allowedValues.description: Prevented/Not allowed. Disabling doesn't prevent sideloading of extensions using Add-AppxPackage via Powershell. To prevent this, set the ApplicationManagement/AllowDeveloperUnlock policy to 1 (enabled).

nodes.name: AllowSmartScreen
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you configure whether to turn on Windows Defender SmartScreen.

allowedValues.description: Turned off. Don't protect users from potential threats and prevent users from turning it on.
Turned on. Protect users from potential threats and prevent users from turning it off.

nodes.name: AllowTabPreloading
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether Microsoft Edge can load the Start and New Tab page during Windows sign in and each time Microsoft Edge is closed.

allowedValues.description: Allowed. Preload Start and New tab pages.

nodes.name: AllowWebContentOnNewTabPage
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you configure what appears when Microsoft Edge opens a new tab. By default, Microsoft Edge opens the New Tab page.

allowedValues.description: Load a blank page instead of the default New tab page and prevent users from changing it.
Load the default New tab page.

nodes.name: AlwaysEnableBooksLibrary
nodes.description: This policy setting helps you to decide whether to make the Books tab visible, regardless of a device's country or region setting, as configured in the Country or region area of Windows settings.

allowedValues.description: Show the Books Library only in countries or regions where supported.
Show the Books Library, regardless of the device's country or region.

nodes.name: ClearBrowsingDataOnExit
nodes.description: This policy setting allows the automatic clearing of browsing data when Microsoft Edge closes. If you enable this policy setting, clearing browsing history on exit's turned on.

allowedValues.description: Prevented/not allowed. Users can configure the 'Clear browsing data' option in Settings.
Allowed. Clear the browsing data upon exit automatically.

nodes.name: ConfigureAdditionalSearchEngines
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you add up to 5 additional search engines, which can't be removed by your employees, but can be made a personal default engine.

nodes.name: ConfigureFavoritesBar
nodes.description: The favorites bar shows your user's links to sites they've added to it. With this policy, you can specify whether to set the favorites bar to always be visible or hidden on any page.

allowedValues.description: Hide the favorites bar on all pages. Also, the favorites bar toggle, in Settings, is set to Off and disabled preventing users from making changes. Microsoft Edge also hides the “show bar/hide bar” option in the context menu.

Show the favorites bar on all pages. Also, the favorites bar toggle, in Settings, is set to On and disabled preventing users from making changes. Microsoft Edge also hides the “show bar/hide bar” option in the context menu.

nodes.name: ConfigureHomeButton
nodes.description: The Home button loads either the default Start page, the New tab page, or a URL defined in the Set Home Button URL policy.

allowedValues.description: Show home button and load the Start page.
Show home button and load the New tab page.
Show home button and load the custom URL defined in the Set Home Button URL policy.

nodes.name: ConfigureKioskMode
nodes.description: Configure how Microsoft Edge behaves when it's running in kiosk mode with assigned access, either as a single app or as one of multiple apps running on the kiosk device.

nodes.name: ConfigureKioskResetAfterIdleTimeout
nodes.description: You can configure Microsoft Edge to reset to the configured start experience after a specified amount of idle time. The reset timer begins after the last user interaction.

nodes.name: ConfigureOpenMicrosoftEdgeWith
nodes.description: You can configure Microsoft Edge to lock down the Start page, preventing users from changing or customizing it.

allowedValues.description: Load a specific page or pages.

nodes.name: ConfigureTelemetryForMicrosoft365Analytics
nodes.description: You can configure Microsoft Edge to send intranet history only, internet history only, or both to Desktop Analytics for enterprise devices with a configured Commercial ID. If disabled or not…

allowedValues.description: Send both intranet and Internet history.

nodes.name: DisableLockdownOfStartPages
nodes.description: You can configure Microsoft Edge to disable the lockdown of Start pages allowing users to change or customize their start pages.

allowedValues.description: Lock down Start pages configured in either the ConfigureOpenEdgeWith policy and HomePages policy.
Unlocked. Users can make changes to all configured start pages.

nodes.name: EnableExtendedBooksTelemetry
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide how much data to send to Microsoft about the book you're reading from the Books tab in Microsoft Edge.

allowedValues.description: Gather and send only basic diagnostic data, depending on the device configuration.

nodes.name: EnterpriseModeSiteList
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you configure whether to use Enterprise Mode and the Enterprise Mode Site List to address common compatibility problems with legacy apps.

nodes.name: EnterpriseSiteListServiceUrl
nodes.description: Important. Discontinued in Windows 10, version 1511. Use the Browser/EnterpriseModeSiteList policy instead.

nodes.name: FirstRunURL
nodes.description: Configure first run URL.

nodes.name: HomePages
nodes.description: When you enable the Configure Open Microsoft Edge With policy, you can configure one or more Start pages. When you enable this policy, users aren't allowed to make changes to their Start pages.

nodes.name: LockdownFavorites
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can add, import, sort, or edit the Favorites list on Microsoft Edge.

allowedValues.description: Allowed/not locked down. Users can add, import, and make changes to the favorites.

nodes.name: PreventAccessToAboutFlagsInMicrosoftEdge
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can access the about:flags page, which is used to change developer settings and to enable experimental features.

allowedValues.description: Prevents users from accessing the about:flags page.

nodes.name: PreventCertErrorOverrides
nodes.description: Web security certificates are used to ensure a site your users go to is legitimate, and in some circumstances encrypts the data.

allowedValues.description: Allowed/turned on. Override the security warning to sites that have SSL errors.

nodes.name: PreventFirstRunPage
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees see Microsoft's First Run webpage when opening Microsoft Edge for the first time.

allowedValues.description: Allowed. Load the First Run webpage.

nodes.name: PreventLiveTileDataCollection
nodes.description: This policy lets you decide whether Microsoft Edge can gather Live Tile metadata from the ieonline.microsoft.com service to provide a better experience while pinning a Live Tile to the Start menu.

allowedValues.description: Collect and send Live Tile metadata.

nodes.name: PreventSmartScreenPromptOverride
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can override the Windows Defender SmartScreen warnings about potentially malicious websites.

allowedValues.description: Allowed/turned off. Users can ignore the warning and continue to the site.

nodes.name: PreventSmartScreenPromptOverrideForFiles
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether employees can override the Windows Defender SmartScreen warnings about downloading unverified files.

allowedValues.description: Allowed/turned off. Users can ignore the warning and continue to download the unverified file(s).

nodes.name: PreventTurningOffRequiredExtensions
nodes.description: You can define a list of extensions in Microsoft Edge that users cannot turn off. You must deploy extensions through any available enterprise deployment channel, such as Microsoft Intune.

nodes.name: PreventUsingLocalHostIPAddressForWebRTC
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether an employee's LocalHost IP address shows while making calls using the WebRTC protocol.

nodes.name: ProvisionFavorites
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to configure a default set of favorites, which will appear for employees. Employees can't modify, sort, move, export or delete these provisioned favorites.

nodes.name: SendIntranetTraffictoInternetExplorer
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether your intranet sites should all open using Internet Explorer 11.

allowedValues.description: All sites, including intranet sites, open in Microsoft Edge automatically.
Only intranet sites open in Internet Explorer 11 automatically.

nodes.name: SetDefaultSearchEngine
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you configure the default search engine for your employees. Your employees can change the default search engine at any time. Important.

nodes.name: SetHomeButtonURL
nodes.description: The home button can be configured to load a custom URL when your user clicks the home button.

nodes.name: SetNewTabPageURL
nodes.description: You can set the default New Tab page URL in Microsoft Edge. Enabling this policy prevents your users from changing the New tab page setting.

nodes.name: ShowMessageWhenOpeningSitesInInternetExplorer
nodes.description: You can configure Microsoft Edge to open a site automatically in Internet Explorer 11 and choose to display a notification before the site opens.

allowedValues.description: Show an additional message stating that a site has opened in IE11.
Show an additional message with a "Keep going in Microsoft Edge" link.

nodes.name: SyncFavoritesBetweenIEAndMicrosoftEdge
nodes.description: This setting lets you decide whether people can sync their favorites between Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge.

nodes.name: UnlockHomeButton
nodes.description: By default, when enabling Configure Home Button or Set Home Button URL, the home button is locked down to prevent your users from changing what page loads when clicking the home button.

allowedValues.description: Lock down and prevent users from making changes to the settings.

nodes.name: UseSharedFolderForBooks
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you decide whether Microsoft Edge stores books from the Books tab to a default, shared folder for Windows.

allowedValues.description: Prevented/not allowed, but Microsoft Edge downloads book files to a per-user folder for each user.

Allowed. Microsoft Edge downloads book files to a shared folder. For this policy to work correctly, you must also enable the Allow a Windows app to share application data between users group policy. Also, the users must be signed in with a school or work account.

nodes.name: AllowCamera
nodes.description: This policy setting allow the use of Camera devices on the machine. If you enable or don't configure this policy setting, Camera devices will be enabled.

nodes.name: ConfigureCameraOptions
nodes.description: This policy will allow camera mode to be managed by IT admins and enable camera to run in safe or auto share mode.

allowedValues.description: AutoShare - Allow camera access by multiple applications simultaneously.
SafeMode - The camera is configured to auto‑share and operate in a non‑accelerated mode, bypassing OEM/IHV‑provided plugins where applicable.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCellularData
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access cellular data. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCellularData_ForceAllowTheseApps
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access cellular data. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCellularData_ForceDenyTheseApps
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access cellular data. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCellularData_UserInControlOfTheseApps

nodes.name: AllowEdgeSwipe

nodes.name: AllowICMPRedirectsToOverrideOSPFGeneratedRoutes

nodes.name: IPv6SourceRoutingProtectionLevel
nodes.description: IPv6 source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing).

Enabled. Force enable auto-update over metered connection.

nodes.description: Disables the automatic download and update of map data. After the policy is applied, you can verify the settings in the user interface in System > Offline Maps.

nodes.name: AllowCrashDump
nodes.description: This policy setting decides if crash dump collection on the machine is allowed or not. Supported values: 0 - Disable crash dump collection. 1 (default) - Allow crash dump collection.

nodes.name: AllowLiveDump
nodes.description: This policy setting decides if live dump collection on the machine is allowed or not. Supported values: 0 - Disable live dump collection. 1 (default) - Allow live dump collection.

nodes.name: AllowMMS
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to enable or disable the sending and receiving cellular MMS messages.

nodes.name: AllowMessageSync
nodes.description: This policy setting allows backup and restore of cellular text messages to Microsoft's cloud services.

allowedValues.description: Message sync isn't allowed and can't be changed by the user.
Message sync is allowed. The user can change this setting.

nodes.name: AllowRCS
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to enable or disable the sending and receiving of cellular RCS (Rich Communication Services) messages.

nodes.name: AADGroupMembershipCacheValidityInDays

nodes.name: AllowCaptivePortalBeforeLogon
nodes.description: This policy controls whether the device will display the captive portal flow on the HoloLens sign in screen's network selection page when a captive portal network is detected.

nodes.name: AllowLaunchUriInSingleAppKiosk
nodes.description: By default, launching applications via Launcher API is disabled in single app kiosk mode. To enable applications to launch in single app kiosk mode on HoloLens devices, set the policy value to true.

Applications are allowed to be launched with Launcher API, when in single app kiosk mode.

nodes.name: AutoLogonUser
nodes.description: This policy controls whether a user will be automatically logged on. When the policy is set to a non-empty value, it specifies the email address of the auto-logon user.

nodes.name: AutoUnlock
nodes.description: This policy controls whether a signed-in user will be prompted for credentials when returning to the device after the device has entered suspended state.

allowedValues.description: User will be prompted for credentials.
User won't be prompted for credentials.

nodes.name: AutomaticDisplayAdjustment
nodes.description: This policy controls if the HoloLens displays will be automatically adjusted for your eyes to improve hologram visual quality when a user wears the device.

nodes.name: BrightnessButtonDisabled
nodes.description: This policy setting controls if pressing the brightness button changes the brightness or not.

allowedValues.description: Brightness can be changed with press of brightness button.
Brightness can't be changed with press of brightness button.

nodes.name: ConfigureDeviceStandbyAction
nodes.description: This policy setting controls device maintenance action during standby.

nodes.name: ConfigureDeviceStandbyActionTimeout
nodes.description: This policy setting controls when to start maintenance action after device enters standby. The timeout value is in hours.

nodes.name: ConfigureMovingPlatform
nodes.description: This policy controls the behavior of moving platform feature on HoloLens 2, that is, whether it's turned off / on or it can be toggled by a user.

allowedValues.description: Last set user's preference. Initial state is OFF and after that user's preference is persisted across reboots and is used to initialize the system.
Moving platform is disabled and can't be changed by user.
Moving platform is enabled and can't be changed by user.

nodes.name: ConfigureNtpClient
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies a set of parameters for controlling the Windows NTP Client. If you enable this policy setting, you can specify the following parameters for the Windows NTP Client.

nodes.name: ConfigureSharedAccount
nodes.description: This policy specifies the configuration for Shared Accounts on the device.

nodes.name: DisallowNetworkConnectivityPassivePolling
nodes.description: Network Connection Status Indicator (NCSI) detects Internet connectivity and corporate network connectivity status. This policy allows IT admins to disable NCSI passive polling. Value type is integer.

nodes.name: EnableStartMenuSingleHandGesture

allowedValues.description: Don't allow pinching your thumb and index finger, while looking at the Start icon on your wrist, to open the Start menu.
Allow pinching your thumb and index finger, while looking at the Start icon on your wrist, to open the Start menu.

nodes.name: EnableStartMenuVoiceCommand
nodes.description: This policy setting controls if using voice commands to open the Start menu is enabled or not.

allowedValues.description: Using voice commands to open the Start menu is disabled.
Using voice commands to open the Start menu is enabled.

nodes.name: EnableStartMenuWristTap
nodes.description: This policy setting controls if tapping the Star icon on your wrist to open the Start menu is enabled or not.

allowedValues.description: Don't allow tapping the Start icon on your wrist to open the Start menu.
Allow tapping the Start icon on your wrist to open the Start menu.

nodes.name: EyeTrackingCalibrationPrompt

allowedValues.description: Not allowed. Diagnostic logs can't be collected by pressing the button combination.
Allowed for device owners only. Diagnostics logs can be collected by pressing the button combination only if signed-in user is considered as device owner.
Allowed for all users. Diagnostic logs can be collected by pressing the button combination.

nodes.name: HeadTrackingMode

allowedValues.description: (Default) Feature - Default feature based / SLAM-based tracker.

nodes.name: ManualDownDirectionDisabled
nodes.description: This policy controls whether the user can change down direction manually or not. If no down direction is set by the user, then an automatically calculated down direction is used by the system.

allowedValues.description: User is allowed to manually change down direction.
User isn't allowed to manually change down direction.

nodes.name: MicrophoneDisabled
nodes.description: This policy setting controls whether microphone on HoloLens 2 is disabled or not.

allowedValues.description: Microphone can be used for voice.
Microphone can't be used for voice.

nodes.name: NtpClientEnabled

nodes.name: PreferLogonAsOtherUser

allowedValues.description: Don't require the Start icon to be pressed for 2 seconds.
Require the Start icon to be pressed for 2 seconds.

nodes.name: RequireStartIconVisible
nodes.description: This policy setting controls if it's required that the Start icon to be looked at when you tap it to open the Start menu.

allowedValues.description: Don't require the Start icon to be looked at when you tap it.
Require the Start icon to be looked at when you tap it.

nodes.name: SkipCalibrationDuringSetup
nodes.description: This policy configures whether the device will take the user through the eye tracking calibration process during device setup and first time user setup.

allowedValues.description: Eye tracking calibration process will be shown during device setup and first time user setup.
Eye tracking calibration process won't be shown during device setup and first time user setup.

nodes.name: SkipTrainingDuringSetup
nodes.description: This policy configures whether the device will take the user through a training process during device setup and first time user setup.

allowedValues.description: Training process will be shown during device setup and first time user setup.
Training process won't be shown during device setup and first time user setup.

nodes.name: VisitorAutoLogon
nodes.description: This policy controls whether a visitor user will be automatically logged in. Visitor users can only be created and logged in, if an Assigned Access profile has been created targeting visitor users.

allowedValues.description: Visitor user won't be signed in automatically.
Visitor user will be signed in automatically.

nodes.name: VolumeButtonDisabled

allowedValues.description: Volume can be changed with press of the volume button.
Volume can't be changed with press of the volume button.

nodes.name: BrowserAltTabBlowout

allowedValues.description: Open windows and all tabs in Microsoft Edge.
Open windows and 5 most recent tabs in Microsoft Edge.
Open windows and 3 most recent tabs in Microsoft Edge.

nodes.description: This policy setting turns off tile notifications. If you enable this policy setting, applications and system features won't be able to update their tiles and tile badges in the Start screen.

nodes.name: AllowStandbyWhenSleepingPluggedIn

nodes.name: SelectPowerButtonActionPluggedIn

nodes.name: SelectSleepButtonActionPluggedIn
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies the action that Windows takes when a user presses the sleep button. Possible actions include: -Take no action -Sleep -Hibernate -Shut down.

nodes.name: ApprovedUsbPrintDevicesUser

nodes.description: Determines whether to always send page count information for accounting purposes for printers using the Microsoft IPP Class Driver.

nodes.name: ConfigureIppTlsCertificatePolicy

nodes.description: Determines whether Redirection Guard is enabled for the print spooler. You can enable this setting to configure the Redirection Guard policy being applied to spooler.

nodes.description: This policy setting controls which protocols incoming RPC connections to the print spooler are allowed to use.

nodes.name: EnableDeviceControlUser
nodes.description: Determines whether Device Control Printing Restrictions are enforced for printing on this computer. By default, there are no restrictions to printing based on connection type or printer Make/Model.

nodes.name: ManageDriverExclusionList

nodes.name: PointAndPrintRestrictions_User
nodes.description: This policy setting controls the client Point and Print behavior, including the security prompts for Windows Vista computers.

nodes.name: PublishPrinters

nodes.name: RequireIppsPolicy

nodes.name: RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators
nodes.description: Determines whether users that aren't Administrators can install print drivers on this computer. By default, users that aren't Administrators can't install print drivers on this computer.

nodes.name: AllowAutoAcceptPairingAndPrivacyConsentPrompts
nodes.description: Allows or disallows the automatic acceptance of the pairing and privacy user consent dialog when launching apps. Most restricted value is 0.

nodes.name: AllowCrossDeviceClipboard
nodes.description: This policy setting determines whether Clipboard contents can be synchronized across devices.

nodes.name: AllowInputPersonalization
nodes.description: This policy specifies whether users on the device have the option to enable online speech recognition services.

nodes.name: DisableAdvertisingId

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessBackgroundSpatialPerception_UserInControlOfTheseApps
nodes.description: List of semi-colon delimited Package Family Names of Windows Store Apps. The user is able to control the user movements privacy setting for the listed apps.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCalendar

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCalendar_ForceAllowTheseApps
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access the calendar. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCalendar_ForceDenyTheseApps
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access the calendar. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LetAppsAccessCalendar_UserInControlOfTheseApps
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Windows apps can access the calendar. You can specify either a default setting for all apps or a per-app setting by specifying a Package Family Name.

nodes.name: LoadAadCredKeyFromProfile

nodes.name: AllowUsersToConnectRemotely
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to configure remote access to computers by using Remote Desktop Services.

nodes.name: ClientConnectionEncryptionLevel

nodes.name: DisconnectOnLockLegacyAuthn

nodes.name: DisconnectOnLockMicrosoftIdentityAuthn
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to configure the user experience when the Remote Desktop session is locked by the user or by a policy.

nodes.name: DoNotAllowDriveRedirection

nodes.name: DoNotAllowPasswordSaving

nodes.name: DoNotAllowWebAuthnRedirection
nodes.description: This policy setting lets you control the redirection of web authentication (WebAuthn) requests from a Remote Desktop session to the local device.

nodes.name: LimitClientToServerClipboardRedirection
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to restrict clipboard data transfers from client to server.

nodes.name: LimitServerToClientClipboardRedirection
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to restrict clipboard data transfers from server to client.

nodes.name: PromptForPasswordUponConnection
nodes.description: This policy setting specifies whether Remote Desktop Services always prompts the client for a password upon connection.

nodes.name: RequireSecureRPCCommunication
nodes.description: Specifies whether a Remote Desktop Session Host server requires secure RPC communication with all clients or allows unsecured communication.

nodes.name: TS_SERVER_REMOTEAPP_USE_SHELLAPPRUNTIME
nodes.description: This policy setting enables an enhanced shell experience for RemoteApp sessions, offering support for default file associations, Run/RunOnce registry keys, and more.

nodes.name: AllowBasicAuthentication_Client
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client uses Basic authentication. If you enable this policy setting, the WinRM client uses Basic authentication.

nodes.name: AllowBasicAuthentication_Service
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service accepts Basic authentication from a remote client.

nodes.name: AllowCredSSPAuthenticationClient
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client uses CredSSP authentication.

nodes.name: AllowCredSSPAuthenticationService
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service accepts CredSSP authentication from a remote client.

nodes.name: AllowRemoteServerManagement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service automatically listens on the network for requests on the HTTP transport over the default HTTP port.

nodes.name: AllowUnencryptedTraffic_Client
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client sends and receives unencrypted messages over the network.

nodes.name: AllowUnencryptedTraffic_Service
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service sends and receives unencrypted messages over the network.

nodes.name: DisallowDigestAuthentication
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client uses Digest authentication.

nodes.name: DisallowNegotiateAuthenticationClient
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client uses Negotiate authentication.

nodes.name: DisallowNegotiateAuthenticationService
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service accepts Negotiate authentication from a remote client.

nodes.name: DisallowStoringOfRunAsCredentials
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service won't allow RunAs credentials to be stored for any plug-ins.

nodes.name: SpecifyChannelBindingTokenHardeningLevel
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to set the hardening level of the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service with regard to channel binding tokens.

nodes.name: TrustedHosts
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to manage whether the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client uses the list specified in TrustedHostsList to determine if the destination host is a trusted entity.

nodes.name: TurnOnCompatibilityHTTPListener
nodes.description: This policy setting turns on or turns off an HTTP listener created for backward compatibility purposes in the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service.

nodes.name: TurnOnCompatibilityHTTPSListener
nodes.description: This policy setting turns on or turns off an HTTPS listener created for backward compatibility purposes in the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service.

nodes.name: RPCEndpointMapperClientAuthentication
nodes.description: This policy setting controls whether RPC clients authenticate with the Endpoint Mapper Service when the call they're making contains authentication information.

nodes.name: RestrictUnauthenticatedRPCClients
nodes.description: This policy setting controls how the RPC server runtime handles unauthenticated RPC clients connecting to RPC servers. This policy setting impacts all RPC applications.

nodes.name: AllowRemoteShellAccess
nodes.description: This policy setting configures access to remote shells. If you enable or don't configure this policy setting, new remote shell connections are accepted by the server.

nodes.name: MaxConcurrentUsers
nodes.description: This policy setting configures the maximum number of users able to concurrently perform remote shell operations on the system. The value can be any number from 1 to 100.

nodes.name: SpecifyIdleTimeout
nodes.description: This policy setting configures the maximum time in milliseconds remote shell will stay open without any user activity until it's automatically deleted. Any value from 0 to 0x7FFFFFFF can be set.

nodes.name: SpecifyMaxMemory
nodes.description: This policy setting configures the maximum total amount of memory in megabytes that can be allocated by any active remote shell and all its child processes.

nodes.name: SpecifyMaxProcesses
nodes.description: This policy setting configures the maximum number of processes a remote shell is allowed to launch.

nodes.name: SpecifyMaxRemoteShells
nodes.description: This policy setting configures the maximum number of concurrent shells any user can remotely open on the same system.

nodes.name: SpecifyShellTimeout
nodes.description: This policy setting is deprecated and has no effect when set to any state: Enabled, Disabled, or Not Configured.

nodes.name: ConfigureGroupMembership
nodes.description: This security setting allows an administrator to define the members of a security-sensitive (restricted) group.

nodes.name: AllowCloudSearch
nodes.description: Allow search and Cortana to search cloud sources like OneDrive and SharePoint.

nodes.name: AllowCortanaInAAD

nodes.name: AllowFindMyFiles
nodes.description: This feature allows you to disable find my files completely on the machine. This policy controls whether the user can configure search to Find My Files mode.

nodes.name: AllowAutoUpdate
nodes.description: Enables the IT admin to manage automatic update behavior to scan, download, and install updates. Important.

allowedValues.description: Notify the user before downloading the update. This policy is used by the enterprise who wants to enable the end-users to manage data usage. With this option users are notified when there are updates that apply to the device and are ready for download. Users can download and install the updates from the Windows Update control panel.

Auto install the update and then notify the user to schedule a device restart. Updates are downloaded automatically on non-metered networks and installed during "Automatic Maintenance" when the device isn't in use and isn't running on battery power. If automatic maintenance is unable to install updates for two days, Windows Update will install updates immediately. If the installation requires a restart, the end-user is prompted to schedule the restart time. After the update is installed, if the user hasn't scheduled a restart, the device will attempt to restart automatically. The user will be notified about the scheduled restart and can reschedule it if the proposed time is inconvenient. Enabling the end-user to control the start time reduces the risk of accidental data loss caused by applications that don't shutdown properly on restart.

Auto install and restart. Updates are downloaded automatically on non-metered networks and installed during "Automatic Maintenance" when the device isn't in use and isn't running on battery power. If automatic maintenance is unable to install updates for two days, Windows Update will install updates right away. If a restart is required, then the device is automatically restarted when the device isn't actively being used. This is the default behavior for unmanaged devices. Devices are updated quickly, but it increases the risk of accidental data loss caused by an application that doesn't shutdown properly on restart.

Auto install and restart at a specified time. The IT specifies the installation day and time. If no day and time are specified, the default is 3 AM daily. Automatic installation happens at this time and device restart happens after a 15-minute countdown. If the user is logged in when Windows is ready to restart, the user can interrupt the 15-minute countdown to delay the restart.

Auto install and restart without end-user control. Updates are downloaded automatically on non-metered networks and installed during "Automatic Maintenance" when the device isn't in use and isn't running on battery power. If automatic maintenance is unable to install updates for two days, Windows Update will install updates right away. If a restart is required, then the device is automatically restarted when the device isn't actively being used. This setting option also sets the end-user control panel to read-only.

nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables audio input to the Sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, Windows Sandbox will be able to receive audio input from the user.

nodes.name: AllowClipboardRedirection
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables clipboard sharing with the sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, copy and paste between the host and Windows Sandbox are permitted.

nodes.name: AllowMappedFolders
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables mapping folders into sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, mapping folders from the host into Sandbox will be permitted.

nodes.name: AllowNetworking
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables networking in the sandbox. You can disable network access to decrease the attack surface exposed by the sandbox.

nodes.name: AllowPrinterRedirection
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables printer sharing from the host into the Sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, host printers will be shared into Windows Sandbox.

nodes.name: AllowVGPU
nodes.description: This policy setting is to enable or disable the virtualized GPU. If you enable this policy setting, vGPU will be supported in the Windows Sandbox.

nodes.name: AllowVideoInput
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables video input to the Sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, video input is enabled in Windows Sandbox.

nodes.name: AllowWriteToMappedFolders
nodes.description: This policy setting enables or disables mapping folders into sandbox. If you enable this policy setting, mapping folders from the host into Sandbox will be permitted.

nodes.name: AllowMdnsAdvertisement
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to turn off the Wireless Display multicast DNS service advertisement from a Wireless Display receiver.

nodes.name: AllowMdnsDiscovery
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to turn off discovering the display service advertised over multicast DNS by a Wireless Display receiver.

nodes.name: AllowMovementDetectionOnInfrastructure
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to disable the infrastructure movement detection feature.

nodes.name: AllowPCReceiverToBeTCPServer
nodes.description: This policy setting allows a PC acting as a Wireless Display receiver to be a TCP server for the TCP session carrying the projection stream to the receiver.

nodes.name: AllowPCSenderToBeTCPClient
nodes.description: This policy setting allows a PC acting as a Wireless Display sender to be a TCP client for the TCP session carrying the projection stream to the receiver.

nodes.name: AllowProjectionFromPC
nodes.description: This policy allows you to turn off projection from a PC. If you set it to 0, your PC can't discover or project to other devices. If you set it to 1, your PC can discover and project to other devices.

allowedValues.description: Your PC can't discover or project to other devices.
Your PC can discover and project to other devices.

nodes.name: AllowProjectionFromPCOverInfrastructure
nodes.description: This policy allows you to turn off projection from a PC over infrastructure.

allowedValues.description: Your PC can't discover or project to other infrastructure devices, although it's possible to discover and project over WiFi Direct.
Your PC can discover and project to other devices over infrastructure.

nodes.name: AllowProjectionToPC
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to turn off projection to a PC. If you turn it on, your PC isn't discoverable and can't be projected to except if the user manually launches the Wireless Display app.

allowedValues.description: Projection to PC isn't allowed. Always off and the user can't enable it.
Projection to PC is allowed. Enabled only above the lock screen.

nodes.name: AllowProjectionToPCOverInfrastructure
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to turn off projection to a PC over infrastructure.

allowedValues.description: Your PC isn't discoverable and other devices can't project to it over infrastructure, although it's possible to project to it over WiFi Direct.
Your PC is discoverable and other devices can project to it over infrastructure.

nodes.name: AllowUserInputFromWirelessDisplayReceiver
nodes.description: Setting this policy controls whether or not the wireless display can send input-keyboard, mouse, pen, and touch input if the display supports it-back to the source device.

nodes.name: RequirePinForPairing
nodes.description: This policy setting allows you to require a pin for pairing. If you set this to 'Never', a pin isn't required for pairing.

allowedValues.description: Pairing ceremony for new devices will always require a PIN.

nodes.name: PrinterProvisioning
nodes.description: Printer Provisioning

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls
nodes.description: This setting will take the action on the specified user account to install or uninstall the specified printer. Install action is selected by default.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}
nodes.description: Identifies the Universal Print printer, by its Share ID, you wish to install on the targeted user account.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}/CloudDeviceID
nodes.description: Identifies the Universal Print printer, by its Printer ID, you wish to install on the targeted user account.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}/ErrorCode
nodes.description: HRESULT of the last installation returned code.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}/Install
nodes.description: Support async execute. Install Universal Print printer.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}/PrinterSharedName
nodes.description: Identifies the Universal Print printer, by its Share Name, you wish to install on the targeted user account.

nodes.name: UPPrinterInstalls/{PrinterSharedID}/Status
nodes.description: 1 finished installation successfully, 2 installation in progress after receiving execute cmd, 4 installation failed, 8 installation initial status, 32 unknown (not used).

nodes.name: Reboot
nodes.description: The root node for the Reboot configuration service provider.

nodes.name: RebootNow
nodes.description: This node executes a reboot of the device. RebootNow triggers a reboot within 5 minutes to allow the user to wrap up any active work.

nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.description: The supported operation is Get.

nodes.name: Schedule/DailyRecurrent
nodes.description: Value in ISO8601 date and time format (such as 2025-10-07T10:35:00) is required.

nodes.name: Schedule/Single
nodes.description: Value in ISO8601 date and time format (such as 2025-10-07T10:35:00) is required. Both the date and time are required. A reboot will be scheduled to occur at the specified date and time.

nodes.name: Schedule/WeeklyRecurrent
nodes.description: Value in ISO8601 date and time format (such as 2025-10-07T10:35:00) is required.

nodes.name: Recovery

nodes.name: NetworkSettings/Wifi
nodes.description: Interior node containing Wi-Fi-related WinRE network settings.

nodes.name: NetworkSettings/Wifi/ReuseWifiSavedOnDevice
nodes.description: When enabled, WinRE will reuse Wi-Fi profiles already saved on the device for network connectivity during recovery.

allowedValues.description: Reuse Wi-Fi profiles saved on the device
Do not reuse Wi-Fi profiles saved on the device

nodes.name: NetworkSettings/Wifi/{SSID}

nodes.name: NetworkSettings/Wifi/{SSID}/WlanXML
nodes.description: XML describing the Wi-Fi network configuration, following the Windows WLAN profile schema. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/nativewifi/wlan-profileschema-schema

nodes.name: PointInTimeRestore
nodes.description: Interior node containing settings related to point-in-time restore.

nodes.name: PointInTimeRestore/EnablePointInTimeRestore
nodes.description: Enable or disable point-in-time restore, a feature that creates restore points to allow restoration to a previous state.

nodes.name: PointInTimeRestore/SetMaxDiskUsage
nodes.description: Refers to the maximum disk space in megabytes that can be used for all restore points. This setting only takes effect if point-in-time restore is enabled.

nodes.name: PointInTimeRestore/SetRestorePointFrequency
nodes.description: Refers to the frequency in minutes at which restore points are automatically created. This setting controls how often the system captures the state for point-in-time restore.

nodes.name: PointInTimeRestore/SetRestorePointRetention
nodes.description: Refers to the retention period in minutes for a restore point. This setting controls how long snapshots are kept before being automatically deleted.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery
nodes.description: Interior node containing settings related to quick machine recovery.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery/AutoRemediationSettings
nodes.description: Interior node containing settings related to auto remediation. Delete on this node will reset all auto remediation settings to their default values.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery/AutoRemediationSettings/EnableAutoRemediation
nodes.description: Enable to automatically check for remediation solutions. Disable to check manually.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery/AutoRemediationSettings/SetRetryInterval
nodes.description: Refers to the time in minutes that a device will wait before trying to look for solutions again.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery/AutoRemediationSettings/SetTimeToReboot
nodes.description: Refers to the time in minutes that a device will spend in the recovery environment before attempting to reboot.

nodes.name: QuickMachineRecovery/EnableQuickMachineRecovery
nodes.description: Enable or disable quick machine recovery, a feature that will search for device recovery solutions if your device fails to start.

nodes.name: RemoteRemediation

nodes.description: Interior node containing settings related to auto remediation. Delete on this node will reset all auto remediation settings to their default values.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/AutoRemediationSettings/EnableAutoRemediation
nodes.description: Enable to automatically check for remediation solutions. Disable to check manually.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/AutoRemediationSettings/SetRetryInterval
nodes.description: Refers to the time in minutes that a device will wait before trying to look for solutions again.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/AutoRemediationSettings/SetTimeToReboot
nodes.description: Refers to the time in minutes that a device will spend in the recovery environment before attempting to reboot.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/EnableCloudRemediation
nodes.description: Enable or disable quick machine recovery, a feature that will search for device recovery solutions if your device fails to start.

nodes.description: Interior node containing settings related to network credentials.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/NetworkSettings/NetworkCredentials/NetworkPassword
nodes.description: Refers to the password for the wifi network that the device will attempt to connect to during remediation. If a password is set without a SSID, then this will be ignored.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/NetworkSettings/NetworkCredentials/NetworkPasswordEncryptionStore
nodes.description: The encryption store that is specified if we are using a custom certificate for password encryption.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/NetworkSettings/NetworkCredentials/NetworkPasswordEncryptionType
nodes.description: Refers to the type of encryption that can be used for the network password. If you specify "Encrypt with custom certificate" you must also enter the encryption store.

nodes.name: CloudRemediationSettings/NetworkSettings/NetworkCredentials/NetworkSSID
nodes.description: Refers to the wifi network SSID that the device will attempt to automatically connect to during remediation.

nodes.name: RemoteWipe

nodes.name: doWipe

nodes.name: doWipePersistProvisionedData
nodes.description: Exec on this node will back up provisioning data to a persistent location and perform a remote wipe on the device.

nodes.name: doWipePersistUserData
nodes.description: Exec on this node will perform a remote reset on the device and persist user accounts and data. The return status code shows whether the device accepted the Exec command.

nodes.name: doWipeProtected
nodes.description: Exec on this node will perform a remote wipe on the device and fully clean the internal drive. In some device configurations, this command may leave the device unable to boot.

nodes.description: Count of operational eSIM profiles stored in the eUICC.

nodes.name: Status/eSIMprofilesMatched
nodes.description: Count of operational eSIM profiles stored on the eUICC whose PLMN ID matches one of the ConnectionProfileIDs setup under the ConnectionProfiles node.

nodes.name: eUICCs
nodes.description: Subtree for all embedded UICCs (eUICC)

nodes.name: {eUICC}
nodes.description: Represents information associated with an eUICC. There is one subtree for each known eUICC, created by the Local Profile Assistant (LPA) when the eUICC is first seen.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Actions
nodes.description: Actions that can be performed on the eUICC as a whole.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Actions/ResetToFactoryState
nodes.description: This triggers an eUICC Memory Reset, which erases all the eSIM profiles in the eUICC.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Actions/Status
nodes.description: Status of most recent operation, as an HRESULT. S_OK indicates success, S_FALSE indicates operation is in progress, other values represent specific errors.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers
nodes.description: Represents servers used for bulk provisioning and eSIM discovery.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}
nodes.description: Node representing a bulk download/discovery server. The node name is the fully qualified domain name of the server that will be used. Creation of this subtree triggers a discovery request.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/AutoEnable
nodes.description: Indicates whether the discovered profile must be enabled automatically after install. This must be set by the MDM when the ServerName subtree is created.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/DiscoveryState
nodes.description: Current state of the discovery operation for this server (Requested = 1, Executing = 2, Completed = 3, Failed = 4).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/ErrorDetail
nodes.description: Detailed error if the profile download and install procedure failed (None = 0, CardGeneralFailure = 1, ConfirmationCodeIncorrect = 2, ConfirmationCodeMissing = 3, ConfirmationCodeMaxRetriesExceeded =…

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/ICCID
nodes.description: The ICCID of the eSIM profile downloaded as a result of successfully running the eSIM bulk activation process policy.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/IsDiscoveryServer
nodes.description: Indicates whether the server is a discovery server or if it is used for bulk download. A discovery server is used every time a user requests a profile discovery operation.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/DownloadServers/{ServerName}/MaximumAttempts
nodes.description: How many times profile download should be attempted before giving up. A value of 0 indicates unlimited retry attempts.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Identifier
nodes.description: The unique eUICC identifier (EID).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/IsActive
nodes.description: Indicates whether this eUICC is physically present and active. Updated only by the LPA.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/PPR1Allowed
nodes.description: Indicates whether the download of a profile with Profile Policy Rule 1 (PPR1) is allowed.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/PPR1AlreadySet
nodes.description: Indicates whether the eUICC has already a profile with Profile Policy Rule 1 (PPR1).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Policies
nodes.description: Device policies associated with the eUICC as a whole (not per-profile).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Policies/LocalUIEnabled
nodes.description: Determines whether or not the user can make changes to the eSIM through the user interface.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles
nodes.description: Represents all enterprise-owned eSIM profiles.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}
nodes.description: Node representing an enterprise-owned eSIM profile. The node name is the ICCID of the profile (which is a unique identifier).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/ErrorDetail
nodes.description: Detailed error if the profile download and install procedure failed (None = 0, CardGeneralFailure = 1, ConfirmationCodeMissing = 3, ForbiddenByPolicy = 5, InvalidMatchingId = 6,…

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/IsEnabled
nodes.description: Indicates whether this eSIM profile is enabled. Can be set by both the MDM and the CSP.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/MatchingID
nodes.description: Matching ID (activation code token) for eSIM profile download. Must be set by the MDM when the ICCID subtree is created.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/PPR1Set
nodes.description: Profile Policy Rule 1 (PPR1) indicates whether disabling of this profile is not allowed (true if not allowed, false otherwise).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/PPR2Set
nodes.description: Profile Policy Rule 2 (PPR2) indicates whether deletion of this profile is not allowed (true if not allowed, false otherwise).

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/ServerName
nodes.description: Fully qualified domain name of the server that can download this eSIM profile. Must be set by the MDM when the ICCID subtree is created.

nodes.name: {eUICC}/Profiles/{ICCID}/State
nodes.description: Current state of the eSIM profile (Installing = 1, Installed = 2, Deleting = 3, Error = 4).
